title: TTF Holds €44 as Ceasefire Dance Enters Decisive Phase — But War Premium Refuses to Die
hook: TTF closed at €44.21/MWh (close 08 Fri) — barely moved on the week despite exchange of fire between US and Iran. Henry Hub at $2.82 — still a different planet. JKM drops to $16.84.
authorWord: The market is gridlocked. Every bullish catalyst (Hormuz closed 69 days, US-Iran fire exchange) is met with a bearish one (MOU progress, Trump 'war terminated'). This is a coiled spring — the break will be violent.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
TTF front-month closed at €44.21/MWh (close 08 May, Thu), ▲+0.55 vs prev week, per Trading Economics / ICE Endex. Over the past month, TTF is down 5.46% but remains +26.14% YoY. NBP settled at 107.87 GBp/thm (close 08 May), ▲+0.94% on the day, down 7.61% on the month, per ICE NBP data. The market is in a holding pattern: neither the ceasefire optimists nor the escalation bears can establish control.

Hormuz Day 69+ and still effectively closed. As of early May 2026, the Strait has been shut to commercial shipping for 69+ days after a failed brief reopening on April 21-22 that collapsed within 24 hours, per Discovery Alert. The House of Commons Library confirms that while a conditional ceasefire is in place, "almost no shipping has used the strait and it remains effectively closed". About 20,000 mariners and 2,000 ships remain stranded in the Persian Gulf per IMO reporting.

Across the Atlantic: Henry Hub at $2.82/MMBtu. US natgas futures fell to $2.82, near a four-week high but still depressed, supported by declining output as major producers (EQT) scale back activity, per Trading Economics. Henry Hub spot last reported at $2.67/MMBtu (settle 04 May), per FRED / EIA. US gas rigs at 129, ▲+21 YoY, while the total rig count rose by one to 548 in the week to May 8, per Baker Hughes / BOE Report. The US gas complex remains functionally disconnected from European geopolitical risk.

Asia: JKM falls to $16.84/MMBtu (close 07 May). Down 13.60% on the month but still +47.07% YoY, per Trading Economics. The decline reflects a mix of demand destruction in Asia, new US LNG supply (Golden Pass first cargo), and some expectation of eventual Hormuz resolution. But the JKM-TTF spread remains wide at ~$12-13/MMBtu equivalent, suggesting Asian buyers are still competing hard for non-Qatari spot cargoes.

Brent crude at $100.49/bbl (close 08 May), ▲+4.76% MoM, ▲+57.24% YoY, per Trading Economics. Oil's resilience above $100 — despite ceasefire hopes — signals the market isn't buying the peace narrative either.

Technical levels: TTF support at €43.50 (prior week low), then €40 (psychological, pre-ceasefire levels). Resistance at €46-47 (late April bounce), then €50 (war premium zone). The 5.46% monthly decline with a flat weekly close suggests accumulation around €44. The TTF Dec '26 contract trades near €44.10, indicating a flat curve — no contango incentive for storage injection.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF Volatility — Buy June €40 Put + €50 Call Straddle: With US-Iran fire exchange (07 May), MOU negotiations in progress, and Hormuz still closed, the binary outcome risk is maximal. A straddle at current levels costs ~€2.50-3.00 total premium. Break-even at €37.50 or €53. The payoff is asymmetric: a failed MOU or escalation could push TTF to €60+; a successful deal with Hormuz reopening could see €35. Both legs profit.

2. Short Jun TTF €38 Puts / Long Jun TTF €50 Calls (Risk Reversal): Express a bullish skew cheaply. Collect ~€0.60-0.80 on the €38 put sale (probability of assignment ~15% given Hormuz supply risk), fund a €50 call purchase (~€1.00). Net cost ~€0.20-0.40. Max loss = €38.00 - premium. Unlimited upside above €50. Rationale: the floor under TTF is structural (Hormuz, Russian LNG ban, low storage), while the ceiling is open on escalation.

3. Long JKM-TTF Spread for Q3 2026: If Hormuz partially reopens, Qatar will prioritize higher-priced Asian lifters, widening the JKM-TTF spread from current ~$12 to $15+/MMBtu. Buy JKM Q3 swap, sell TTF Q3 swap. Target spread widening of $3-5. Stop if Hormuz remains fully closed (spreads compress as Europe bids more aggressively for non-Qatari cargoes).

⚡ Dissenting View — Henry 🦉
Trump said Thursday that hostilities have been "terminated" — that's the strongest language yet. The MOU has 14 points and both sides are talking through intermediaries. If a deal lands, TTF doesn't drift lower — it crashes. The €5-8 gap lower I warned about last month never happened because the market is already pricing a deal at 70% probability. But if it goes from 70% to 100%, you're looking at €35-38 in a week.
